{{Navbar-Global Gas Infrastructure Tracker}}
'''Great Basin Gas Transmission Company Pipeline System''' is a natural gas pipeline in the United States, with 6 segments.

==Location==
Main Line: The pipeline runs from Idaho-Nevada border, Nevada to Nevada-California border, Nevada.<ref name="r770e1b">{{Cite web|url=https://www.greatbasingtc.com/|title=https://www.greatbasingtc.com/|website=greatbasingtc.com|access-date=2026-11-05}}</ref><ref name="r30800f">{{Cite web|url=https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/pipelines/EIA-NaturalGasPipelineProjectsAug2026.xlsx|title=Natural Gas Pipeline Projects, U.S. Energy Information Administration, August 2026|website=eia.gov|access-date=2026-11-05}}</ref>
2024 Expansion: The pipeline is located in Nevada.<ref name="ra9e36d">{{Cite web|url=https://expansion2024.greatbasingtcprojects.com/apexpfr204/pfrproddb/pfruser_ws/r/exp24/hp?session=16855456207524|title=https://expansion2024.greatbasingtcprojects.com/apexpfr204/pfrproddb/pfruser_ws/r/exp24/hp?session=16855456207524|website=expansion2024.greatbasingtcprojects.com|access-date=2026-11-05}}</ref><ref name="rc144ec">{{Cite web|url=https://expansion2024.greatbasingtcprojects.com/ords251/pfrprod/r/pfruser_ws/exp24/hp?session=1421675494080|title=https://expansion2024.greatbasingtcprojects.com/ords251/pfrprod/r/pfruser_ws/exp24/hp?session=1421675494080|website=expansion2024.greatbasingtcprojects.com|access-date=2026-11-05}}</ref><ref name="r37fb78">{{Cite web|url=https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2023/05/19/2023-10738/great-basin-gas-transmission-company-notice-of-application-and|title=Great Basin Gas Transmission Company; Notice of Application and, Federal Register, 19 May 2023|website=federalregister.gov|access-date=2026-11-05}}</ref>
Gabbs Lateral NASF Relocation: The pipeline is located in Nevada.<ref name="r5b614c">{{Cite web|url=https://gabbsfnas.greatbasingtcprojects.com/apexpfr204/pfrproddb/f?p=EXP23:HP::::::|title=https://gabbsfnas.greatbasingtcprojects.com/apexpfr204/pfrproddb/f?p=EXP23:HP::::::|website=gabbsfnas.greatbasingtcprojects.com|access-date=2026-11-05}}</ref><ref name="r63b7e0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-03-18/pdf/2026-05271.pdf|title=Federal Register, Vol. 91, No. 52, 18 March 2026, Notices|website=govinfo.gov|access-date=2026-11-05}}</ref>
2026 Expansion: The pipeline is located in Nevada.<ref name="r100d46">{{Cite web|url=https://www.ferc.gov/industries-data/natural-gas/major-pipeline-projects-pending|title=https://www.ferc.gov/industries-data/natural-gas/major-pipeline-projects-pending|website=ferc.gov|access-date=2026-11-05}}</ref><ref name="rb583de">{{Cite web|url=https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2025/05/05/2025-07744/great-basin-gas-transmission-company-notice-of-application-and-establishing-intervention-deadline|title=Great Basin Gas Transmission Company; Notice of Application and Establishing Intervention Deadline, Federal Register, 5 May 2025|website=federalregister.gov|access-date=2026-11-05}}</ref>
2028 Expansion: The pipeline is proposed to run from Winnemucca vicinity, Nevada to west of Fernley, Nevada.<ref name="r30d26d">{{Cite web|url=https://pgjonline.com/news/2025/june/great-basin-gas-expansion-draws-strong-shipper-demand-in-northern-nevada|title=Great Basin Gas Expansion Draws Strong Shipper Demand in Northern Nevada, Pipeline & Gas Journal, 9 June 2025|website=pgjonline.com|access-date=2026-11-05}}</ref><ref name="r5727fc">{{Cite web|url=https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/04/30/2026-08459/great-basin-gas-transmission-company|title=Notice of Scoping Period Requesting Comments on Environmental Issues for the Planned 2028 Expansion Project, Federal Register, 30 April 2026|website=federalregister.gov|access-date=2026-11-05}}</ref><ref name="r4b63c2">{{Cite web|url=https://expansion2028.greatbasingtcprojects.com/ords251/pfrprod/r/pfruser_ws/100/files/static/v59/Great-Basin-Expansion-Project_Fact-Sheet-FINAL_August_2026.pdf|title=Great Basin 2028 Expansion Project fact sheet, August 2026|website=expansion2028.greatbasingtcprojects.com|access-date=2026-11-05}}</ref>
2015 Elko Area Expansion Project: The pipeline runs from Wieland Flat Compressor Station (Ruby Pipeline interconnect), Nevada to Elko City Gate, Nevada.<ref name="r4a3bf2">{{Cite web|url=https://nnbw.com/news/2015/jul/27/blm-oks-natural-gas-pipeline-right-of-way|title=https://nnbw.com/news/2015/jul/27/blm-oks-natural-gas-pipeline-right-of-way|website=nnbw.com|access-date=2026-11-05}}</ref><ref name="rd46939">{{Cite web|url=https://regulations.justia.com/regulations/fedreg/2014/07/21/2014-17046.html|title=https://regulations.justia.com/regulations/fedreg/2014/07/21/2014-17046.html|website=regulations.justia.com|access-date=2026-11-05}}</ref>

==Background==
===Main Line===
Great Basin Gas Transmission Company owns and operates a natural gas pipeline system in Nevada. The company was formerly known as Paiute Pipeline Company and is a wholly owned subsidiary of Southwest Gas Corporation.<ref name="r770e1b" /> In 1963, Southwest Gas built a new transmission line from the Idaho-Nevada border southwest across northern Nevada to the Carson City and Reno-Sparks area and Lake Tahoe.<ref name="r770e1b" /> The system now extends from the Idaho-Nevada border to the Nevada-California border.<ref name="r770e1b" />

A company safety brochure describes the system as 900 miles long. It delivers gas to three local distribution companies and to large customers such as power plants, mines, and processing plants.<ref name="r64fb23" /> A June 2025 trade press report gave the length as 898 miles.<ref name="r30d26d" /> These figures are for the whole system. No source gives a length for the main line alone.

===2024 Expansion===
Great Basin applied to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission on May 1, 2023 to build its 2024 Expansion Project in Nevada.<ref name="r37fb78" /> The project has three parts. Great Basin would build about 0.25 miles of 20-inch pipeline loop along its Carson Lateral in Storey County. It would replace about 2.88 miles of 10-inch pipe with 20-inch pipe along the Carson Lateral in Lyon County. It would also build about 0.28 miles of 12-inch pipeline loop on its South Tahoe Lateral in Douglas County.<ref name="r37fb78" />

The project would provide 5,674 dekatherms per day of added firm transportation service for two existing shippers. Great Basin estimated the cost at $14,939,850.<ref name="r37fb78" /> A Federal Energy Regulatory Commission notice dated November 28, 2023 said staff had prepared an environmental assessment of the project.<ref name="rb8d7d7" /> No source found confirms final approval or construction.

===Gabbs Lateral NASF Relocation===
Great Basin applied to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission on September 29, 2025 to install about 33 miles of new pipeline and abandon about 21 miles of its existing Gabbs Lateral in Nevada. The Gabbs Lateral Naval Air Station Fallon Relocation Project would start about 26 miles east of Schurz and end about 3 miles west-northwest of Gabbs.<ref name="r17324a" />

A Federal Register notice dated March 13, 2026 said Commission staff had prepared an environmental assessment. It described about 32.6 miles of new pipe, made up of 18.8 miles of 8-inch pipe and 13.8 miles of 6-inch pipe. It also described removing about 21.2 miles of existing pipe. The notice said the project would not provide any incremental capacity.<ref name="r63b7e0" /> Great Basin said construction was scheduled to begin on or about March 1, 2027 and be completed by November 1, 2027, subject to approvals.<ref name="r17324a" />

===2026 Expansion===
Great Basin applied to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission on April 15, 2025 to build its 2026 Expansion Project in Lyon and Washoe Counties, Nevada. The project would install about 2.32 miles of new 20-inch pipeline loop along the Carson Lateral, and replace about 2.35 miles of existing 10-inch pipe with new 20-inch pipe.<ref name="rb583de" /> It would add 8,129 dekatherms per day of firm transportation capacity for two existing shippers in northern Nevada and northern California. Great Basin estimated the cost at $18,884,092.<ref name="rb583de" />

A Federal Energy Regulatory Commission notice dated November 25, 2025 said staff had prepared an environmental assessment. It described about 4.7 miles of upsized or looped pipeline in two segments.<ref name="r84f0c2" /> No source found shows that the project was approved or built.

===2028 Expansion===
Great Basin proposed a 2028 Expansion Project to add natural gas capacity in northern Nevada. It opened a binding open season on January 28, 2025 for firm service starting as early as November 1, 2028. The closing date was extended to May 28, 2025.<ref name="r30d26d" /> Southwest Gas Holdings announced on June 5, 2025 that the open season had closed with strong interest. It estimated about 1.25 billion cubic feet per day of new capacity and a cost of $800 million to $1.2 billion.<ref name="r30d26d" />

A Federal Energy Regulatory Commission scoping notice dated April 27, 2026 described about 195 miles of new 42-inch pipeline and about 15 miles of new 24-inch lateral pipelines. The project would include a new Jungo Road Compressor Station. Great Basin planned to abandon about 142 miles of existing pipeline, mostly from the 1960s, plus the Rye Patch and Lovelock Compressor Stations.<ref name="r5727fc" /> A company fact sheet gave about 230 miles of pipeline, up to about 948,000 dekatherms per day of new capacity, and a target in-service date of November 2028.<ref name="r4b63c2" /> A December 2025 letter to the Commission, reported by Nevada Current in June 2026, described 181 miles of new pipeline plus a 14 mile segment, running from near Winnemucca to west of Fernley.<ref name="r8d540a">{{Cite web|url=https://nevadacurrent.com/2026/06/04/lombardo-backs-natural-gas-pipeline-expansion-for-data-centers/|title=Lombardo backs natural gas pipeline expansion for data centers, Nevada Current, 4 June 2026|website=nevadacurrent.com|access-date=2026-11-05}}</ref> The sources differ on the length and the capacity. The project was in planning and development as of 2026.<ref name="r4b63c2" />

===2015 Elko Area Expansion Project===
Paiute Pipeline Company applied to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission to build the project in Elko County, Nevada. The company said it would provide 21,994 dekatherms a day of service.<ref name="rb7ac71" /> The Bureau of Land Management said the project would expand gas capacity to Elko for growing residential and business load and the energy needs of mining operations.<ref name="r4a3bf2" />

The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission issued its certificate on May 14, 2015.<ref name="r4a3bf2" /> In July 2015, the Bureau of Land Management signed a decision record approving a right-of-way for about 35.2 miles of new 8-inch pipe.<ref name="r4a3bf2" />
